How Starr County, Texas, Conducts Tax Sales

Starr County, Texas, holds tax sales to recover unpaid property taxes. Buyers can participate through an organized process designed to ensure fairness and transparency. Below is a detailed guide to how Starr County conducts its tax sales.

Notification and Public Notices

Starr County provides clear notifications about upcoming tax sales. The notices include important details to help buyers prepare.

The county posts notices at least 21 days before the auction date. Notices list the date, time, location, and descriptions of the properties. The auction location is usually 401 N Britton, Rio Grande City, TX, with auctions starting at 10:30 AM. The Starr County Courthouse and the county’s website display these notices for public access.

Check out our Auction Calendar for scheduled auctions.

Registration Requirements

Participants must complete registration with the Starr County Tax Office before they can bid. The registration process includes:

  • Submitting a registration application by the specified deadline.

  • Providing valid identification to verify eligibility.

  • Ensuring no outstanding tax liabilities exist in Starr County.

  • Visiting the Starr County Tax Office, located at 100 N FM 3167, Suite 201, Rio Grande City, TX, for registration assistance.

Preparing for the Auction

Proper preparation is essential for making informed decisions during the auction. To prepare:

  1. Review public notices and property descriptions to identify options.
  2. Investigate the location, condition, and potential value of the properties.
  3. Verify whether properties have liens or encumbrances.
  4. Consult with real estate or legal experts to understand risks and obligations.
  5. Study the auction rules to avoid surprises during bidding.

Auction Day Process

Starr County conducts tax sales at the specified location, following a structured auction process. Here is what happens:

  • The auction begins at 10:30 AM, with registered bidders ready to participate.

  • Bidding starts at the minimum amount, which includes delinquent taxes, penalties, and fees.

  • Winning bidders must pay immediately after the auction concludes.

  • Accepted payment methods include cashier’s checks or other forms specified by the Tax Office.

Post-Auction Responsibilities

After successfully bidding on a property, buyers must complete these steps:

  1. Collect the deed to confirm ownership.
  2. Record the deed with the Starr County Clerk’s office to formalize the transfer.
  3. Resolve any legal or title issues, such as existing liens.
  4. Pay future property taxes on time to maintain ownership.

Redemption Period

Starr County follows Texas law regarding property redemption. Here is what buyers and property owners need to know:

  • Former property owners can redeem homestead and agricultural properties within two years.

  • Other properties have a 180-day redemption period.

To redeem, former owners must pay the purchase price, taxes covered by the buyer, and a premium. The premium increases to 50% in the second year for homestead and agricultural properties.
